test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The weight of an object is the power with which it is attracted towards the earth.
The weight of an object is constant and does not change from place to place.
The mass of an object is constant and does not change from place to place.
The weight is equal to the product of velocity and acceleration due to gravity.

solution:
The correct answer is __**3) The mass of an object is constant and does not change from place to place**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental property of an object that does not change regardless of location.
 
• The **mass** of an object is measured in kilograms (kg) and remains constant whether the object is on Earth, the Moon, or in space.
 
• **Weight**, on the other hand, is the force exerted by gravity on an object and can vary depending on the gravitational pull at different locations.
 
• Mass is a scalar quantity, meaning it only has magnitude, whereas weight is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weight** is calculated using the formula *Weight = Mass × Gravitational Acceleration (W = mg)*.
 
• The gravitational acceleration on Earth is approximately 9.8 m/s², but this value can differ slightly depending on the location.
 
• On the Moon, the gravitational acceleration is about 1/6th of that on Earth, which is why objects weigh less on the Moon.
 
• **Mass** is commonly measured using a balance, which compares an unknown mass to a standard mass.
 
• Inertia is a concept related to mass, describing an object's resistance to changes in its state of motion.
